subject: English
passage:
The following text is adapted from James Baldwin's 1953 novel Go Tell It on the Mountain. Marcus lives in an apartment in Brooklyn, New York.

The morning light was streaming through the windows, casting long shadows across the courtyard. The courtyard looks peaceful at this hour, Marcus thought. It was alive with activity as residents went about their morning routines. An elderly woman was hanging laundry on a clothesline, moving methodically from one piece to the next. Children were walking to school, their voices echoing off the brick walls as they called to friends.

©1953 by James Baldwin
prompt: Which choice best describes what is happening in the text?

choices.A: Marcus is irritated by the noise of residents going about their daily routines in his courtyard.
choices.B: Marcus is observing the appearance of the courtyard at a particular time of day and the events occurring in it.
choices.C: Marcus is confused by the unfamiliar activities taking place in the courtyard.
choices.D: Marcus is staying inside his apartment because he wants to avoid contact with other residents.

explanation:
Choice B is the best answer because it most accurately states what is happening in the text. The narrator notes that Marcus thinks the courtyard looks peaceful in the morning light. The narrator goes on to describe what Marcus can see in the courtyard: a woman hanging laundry and children walking to school.

Why D is incorrect:

Choice D is incorrect because there is no evidence in the text that Marcus wants to avoid contact with other residents or that he is staying inside his apartment. All the text indicates about Marcus is that he is watching the events in the courtyard and thinks it looks peaceful in the morning light.
